title: Research: Operational Outcomes of Phishing-Resistant Authentication in Clinical Settings
summary: A study of phishing-resistant authentication rollouts in clinical environments, examining where workflow friction caused rollbacks and which deployment patterns survived.
content:
## Overview

This post presents findings from our recent research work. A study of phishing-resistant authentication rollouts in clinical environments, examining where workflow friction caused rollbacks and which deployment patterns survived.

**Scope:** Deployment outcome study

**Confidence:** Moderate

## Data and methodology

Self-reported outcomes from participating organisations, with limited independent verification of the reported figures.

## What we observed

- Rollbacks were driven by shared-workstation workflows rather than by user resistance to the authentication method itself.
- Deployments that paired hardware authenticators with badge-tap session resumption were retained; those that did not were frequently reversed.
- Reported credential-phishing incidents fell substantially where the rollout was retained, though self-reporting limits the strength of this conclusion.
